newsitem.title: USA: C-TEC says offers to buy Mercom for stock. [CORRECTED 18:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: C-TEC says offers to buy Mercom for stock. [CORRECTED 18:15 GMT]

text.p: C-TEC Corp said Monday it has offered to acquire 38 percent (corrects from 8.75 percent) of the common stock of Mercom Inc not currently owned by C-TEC.
In exchange, C-TEC said it was offering 23 percent of C-TEC Cable Systems of Michigan Inc, one of the entities expected to be spun off as part of its previously announced restructuring plans.
The proposed exchange ratio is based on the assumption that C-TEC Michigan will have approximately $125 million of net debt outstanding at the time of the transaction.

In the proposed transaction, Mercom would become a wholly owned subsidiary of C-TEC Michigan. The combined operation would serve a total of approximately 200,000 cable television subscribers, approximately 40,000 of which are currently served by Mercom.

David C. McCourt, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of C-TEC, said, "The proposed transaction would allow Mercom shareholders the opportunity to own, in a tax-free exchange, a stock with greater liquidity than the stock they now hold and allow them to share in the prospects of the combined organization. In addition, Mercom and C-TEC shareholders will benefit from the operational and financial flexibility and efficiency that will follow from having this major asset as a wholly-owned subsidiary."
